THING_MODEL.SPECIFICATIONS:
Generic Sensor
Quick way to create a sensor.  Contains a library to setup sensors using only a couple lines of code.

Features:
  • Generic, quick way to setup a variety of sensors.  Setup sensor reading and writing with a single line of script.  Values can be (but don't need to be) written to slots and can modified before sending.
  • Call functions as properties for different setup functions to handle the different ways to detect data.
  • Automatic registration server setup can be used when the sensor is set to write to a slot.
Usage:
The user calls a search parameter specifier function inside of setup().  It sets how the sensor detects information.  This could be environment variables, device properties or devices in range.  It makes the sensor a black box, and the user can respond to the information as needed.  The user can specify how the information is then written to slots or perform data processing before the data is sent to a slot.

There are three main functions:
setup()
loop()
processValues()

setup():
Where you specify what you want the sensor to detect and what it should do with it.  Call one of the library functions for setting up a specific sensor category with the properties to detect.

loop():
Standard update function.  Calls a library function that handles the actual sensing.

processValues():
Called when sensor data has been read.  It receives the read data.  What is returned from the function is what will be sent to a slot if a slot is setup for writing.

There are several categories of sensors.
1: setupDetectEnvironment()
Sets up the sensor to detect an environment property.

// Check for the environment LIGHT value and send it as a analog value to slot 0.
setupDetectEnvironment('LIGHT', createAnalogWrite(0));

2: setupDetectProperty()
Sets up the sensor to detect a property in an IoT device.
It can detect specific devices and devices in some distance of the sensor.

// Finds all devices that have the 'BADGE' property.
setupDetectProperty('BADGE', createPropertySearch());

// Check for a device with the name 'userRedge' and retrieve it's 'BADGE' property.
setupDetectProperty('BADGE', createPropertySearch('userRedge'));

// Check for the two specified devices and get their property values.
setupDetectProperty('BADGE', createPropertySearchDevices(['userRedge', 'userLarry']));

// Search an area of 400x400 around the sensor to detect if the specified device is there and retrieve its value.
setupDetectProperty('BADGE', createPropertySearch('userRedge', 400, 400, 'CENTER'))

Writing to slots:
There are three specifiers for writing to slots.  Each takes the slot number it will write to.
createAnalogWrite()
createDigitalWrite()
createCustomWrite()

Detecting mouse clicking:
After the sensor check is run in update, you can check for  mouse click with getMouseClicked().
This will only return true when the Alt+Click is first detected and will not return true while the button is held.

Registration server setup:
The sensor can detect the type of slot it is writing to (if any) and setup a registration server entry.
The processed sensor value will be sent.

At the end of setup(), call the following function with the text you want displayed in the registration server.
setupRegistrationServer('Sensor Type Here', 'Value Name Here');

Direct Control:
  • N/A
Local Control:
  • Depends on how the sensor is setup.
Remote Control:
  • N/A

Data Specifications:

Any input/output could be used

Example:
This is how the Fire Sensor was setup to check for a property and send information to the Registration Server, using two lines of code.

setupDetectProperty('IR', createPropertySearchDevices(null, 32, -60, 'TOP_LEFT'), createDigitalWrite(0));

setupRegistrationServer('Fire Sensor', 'Fire Detected');
